summary.text: Stereochemistry is the part of chemistry that studies how the atoms in a molecule are arranged in space.
Its main subjects are stereoisomers, which have the same molecular formula and the same sequence of bonded atoms but differ in where the atoms sit in space.
It matters in medicine: ibuprofen exists as (R)- and (S)-isomers, and only the (S) form reduces inflammation and pain.

facts.label: Applies to
facts.value: Organic and inorganic compounds and ions alike

items.prompt: Two molecules have the same formula and the same sequence of bonded atoms, but their atoms sit differently in space. How are they related?

options.label: They have different bonded sequences
They are stereoisomers of each other
They are the same molecule drawn twice
They have different molecular formulas

items.explain: Same formula and same bonded sequence with a different spatial positioning of atoms is what defines stereoisomers.

items.prompt: In a drawing, one bond is shown as a solid wedge. What does that tell you about the bond?

options.label: It lies flat in the plane of the molecule
It recedes away from the viewer
It projects toward the viewer
It has been broken in the reaction

items.explain: A solid wedge marks a bond projecting toward the viewer; a dashed bond recedes and plain lines lie in the plane.

items.prompt: In a Fischer projection, you see a bond drawn horizontally. What does it mean?

options.label: The bond recedes away from the viewer
The bond is a double bond
The bond lies in the plane of the page
The bond projects toward the viewer

items.explain: In a Fischer projection horizontal bonds project toward the viewer and vertical bonds recede away.

items.prompt: A pharmacist argues that giving patients only one of thalidomide's two mirror-image forms would avoid the harm. Why does that fail?

options.label: The body produces the other form from the one given
The one form is destroyed before it acts
Both forms are always harmless on their own
The mirror-image forms are in fact identical

items.explain: Thalidomide undergoes racemization in the body, so the other enantiomer appears even when only one is administered.

items.prompt: A tablet contains ibuprofen, which can exist as two isomers. Which one does the work against pain and inflammation?

options.label: Both isomers equally
The (R) isomer
Neither alone; they must be combined
The (S) isomer

items.explain: Only (S)-ibuprofen is active in reducing inflammation and pain.

items.prompt: Two chemists want to describe the same molecule's stereochemistry in exactly the same way. What do the Cahn–Ingold–Prelog rules give them?

options.label: A standard ranking of atoms around a stereochemical region
A photograph-quality 3D picture of the molecule
A way to change one stereoisomer into another
A count of every atom in the molecule

items.explain: The rules rank the atoms around a stereochemical region in a standard way, which allows unambiguous descriptions of their relative positions.
